---
title: "Depending on anvl"
---

This article is for authors of packages that depend on {anvl}.
It explains why tests that run {anvl} code cannot run on CRAN, how to skip them there, and where they run instead.

## Why PJRT Tests Cannot Run on CRAN

{anvl} compiles and runs programs through PJRT plugins, one for each platform (CPU and CUDA).
The plugins do not come with the {pjrt} package but are downloaded on first use (see the [Installation](installation.html) article), and a non-interactive session such as `R CMD check` downloads them only when the `PJRT_INSTALL` environment variable is `1`.
CRAN's check machines neither have a plugin nor set `PJRT_INSTALL`, so a test that runs {anvl} code on the default `"pjrt"` backend fails there with an error saying that the plugin needs to be downloaded.

## Skipping the Tests

Start each such test with `skip_if_no_pjrt_plugin()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
test_that("my_model() recovers the coefficients", {
  anvl::skip_if_no_pjrt_plugin()
  fit <- my_model(x, y)
  expect_equal(coef(fit), beta, tolerance = 1e-4)
})
```

It skips the test unless the plugin is downloaded, the `PJRT_PLUGIN_PATH_<PLATFORM>` environment variable points to one, or `PJRT_INSTALL=1` allows downloading it.
By default it asks for the plugin of the platform of the default device, which is where a test that names no device runs; a test that needs another one names it, e.g. `skip_if_no_pjrt_plugin("cuda")`.

Use it instead of `skip_on_cran()`.
That one decides by the `NOT_CRAN` environment variable, which says where the check runs, while `skip_if_no_pjrt_plugin()` decides by whether the plugin is there, so the tests run wherever it is.
To run them in your own CI, set `PJRT_INSTALL=1` or call `anvl::install_anvl()` before the check.

## Reverse Dependency Checks

Before each release of {anvl}, we run the reverse dependency checks, `R CMD check` of the packages that depend on {anvl} against the new version, with the PJRT plugins installed.
The tests guarded by `skip_if_no_pjrt_plugin()` therefore run there, even though CRAN skips them, so a change in {anvl} that breaks your package is caught before the release.
